description: Weighted cross-domain unlock graph for the ctrl program (and the sediment sibling repo). Consumed by `./ctrl synergy`. Domain edges say how strongly results in domain A tend to unlock work in domain B. Idea edges connect concrete idea IDs from AGENT_IDEA_INDEX.json and candidate IDs below. Weights are in [0,1] and are directed.

edge_types.certifies: A provides a proof/conditioning guarantee that B's result relies on
edge_types.feeds: A produces the reference signal, model, or data that B consumes
edge_types.composes: A and B are stacked into one closed-loop or pipeline
edge_types.dualizes: A is the mathematical dual of B (same theorem, transposed)
edge_types.benchmarks: A gives the testbed on which B is measured
edge_types.shares_method: A's proof technique transfers directly to B
edge_types.packages: A turns B into a deliverable (kernel, submission, product)

domain_edges.why: DARE/LQR results dualize to the steady-state Kalman filter; detectability and stabilizability swap roles.
Observer and Kalman results close the loop in LQG via the separation principle.
ISS envelopes and H-inf bounds become the outer loop for CLF/CBF designs; MPC terminal sets supply invariant sets.
CBF filters, ZMP allocation and Slotine-Li tracking are the controllers that run on manipulators and legged robots.
Lie-group kinematics give the state manifolds on which CLF/CBF certificates must be stated.
SE(3) kinematics are what visual servoing and pose estimation drive.
Homography/essential decompositions and triangulation deliver the pose feedback for servoing.
Multi-view measurements are the observation model for pose filters and VIO.
Kalman/information fusion stabilizes noisy multi-view pose estimates.
State estimates feed every closed-loop robot controller; POMDP belief planning drives fleets.
Lyapunov-operator conditioning (Byers-Nash) bounds Riccati/Lyapunov sensitivity; matrix identities feed spectral-free proofs.
Same conditioning bounds apply to CARE and Kalman-Bucy.
Spectral-free quadratic-form techniques transfer back to matrix-inequality research.
Covering systems and pinwheel/periodic scheduling share the same CRT density arguments.
Response-time analysis is the WCET/schedulability evidence certification bodies want next to a verified kernel.
Simplex switching gives the architecture in which a verified safety controller takes over.
Reed-Solomon decoding and deadline-bounded cancellation transfer to archive recovery records and cooperative cancellation.
Closed-form CBF/ZMP kernels are the drop-in C99/ST artifacts with the clearest certification story.
Riccati-based gains and ISS margins are what a certified kernel catalog ships.
Zero-heap kernels are what actually runs on robot hardware at 1-10 kHz.
A verified kernel pipeline is grant-shaped (AI for Math Fund tools track, DARPA formal methods programs).
Tactics, Loogle search and the inner loop lower the cost of every new module.
Triage and proof automation are what make the Erdős bounty pipeline cheap.
Submission tooling (lean-verify, Palomar packaging) converts proofs into claims.
Solved-but-unformalized Erdős problems are the direct money lane.
Prize rules (standard axioms, public SHA pinning) shape the tooling.
Aeneas/Verus-style pipelines let the Lean verification habit reach the Rust archive engine.
A hardened, auditable extraction engine is a small worked example of shipping a verified artifact.
Sampled-data stability margins bound the jitter and deadline misses a scheduler may allow.

idea_edges.why: Detectable DARE uniqueness is the dual steady-state Kalman DARE.
DARE gain plus observer gives output-feedback LQG.
P_inf is the MPC terminal cost that makes recursive feasibility and descent go through.
Byers-Nash k(A) <= s(A) controls Lyapunov/Riccati conditioning on the symmetric cone.
Same conditioning bound for CARE and Kalman-Bucy sensitivity.
H-inf Riccati solution is a Stein certificate the Peter-Paul ISS envelope consumes.
ISS sublevel invariants wrap the backstepping/Sontag inner loop.
ISS envelope bounds disturbance entering the CBF safety filter.
Sontag CLF outer loop around Slotine-Li passivity tracking.
Septic trajectory supplies q_r, dq_r, ddq_r for the Slotine-Li regressor.
Energy-optimal reference is the test trajectory of the H-inf/ISS MuJoCo benchmark.
Septic references are the repeated-trial targets ILC refines.
SE(3) centroidal kinematics state the ZMP/CBF constraints.
Jacobians and Lie-group kinematics define the manipulator model.
SE(3) twist kinematics are what the visual-servoing velocity law drives.
Continuous rigid-body kinematics are the process model for Kalman-Bucy on poses.
Four-point homography uniqueness and chirality filtering give the pose used by HBVS.
Triangulated/registered poses are the measurements the Joseph Kalman filter fuses.
Filtered pose stabilizes the servoing loop under measurement noise.
Kalman gain is the observer half of LQG.
Gaussian belief is the continuous analogue of the POMDP belief simplex.
PWLC belief planning plus fleet deadlock graph gives partially-observed fleet scheduling.
Simplex switching and response-time guarantees host the verified CBF backup controller.
CBF shield as terminal safety filter under MPC.
Ackermann/pole placement assigns Luenberger observer poles.
Reachability/observability are the hypotheses of DARE stabilizability/detectability.
Erdős bounty tactics and submission pipeline carry over to #885.
Same pipeline for #273 covering systems.
A closed #885 becomes a new bounty entry.
A closed #273 becomes a new bounty entry.

scoring.description: score = readiness * confidence * (w_nov*novelty/3 + w_app*applicability/3 + w_pay*payoff/5 + w_unlock*tanh(unlock_in/1.5) + w_out*tanh(unlock_out/1.5) + w_pull*pull) - w_eff*log1p(effort_weeks)/log1p(26). unlock_in = sum of incoming idea-edge weights from ready_to_use nodes; unlock_out = sum of outgoing weights; pull = 1 if an external pull is named. With --goal, score is multiplied by 0.25 + 0.75*keyword_overlap(goal, node text); with --domain, by 0.25 + 0.75*max domain->domain weight into the target domains. Readiness: ready_to_use 1.0, promising_near_complete 0.85, in_work 0.7, candidate 0.6.
scoring.rationale: Payoff and unlock-in dominate so that cheap work sitting one edge away from a READY node outranks ambitious isolated work; effort is log-damped so a 12-week project is not crushed, just discounted.
